column1: # THE SHORT FORM FOR A KEY PATTERN: keyed(p, t, e?) means
# match(key(0), p, t, e), with `any` where e is left out (ruling 18 of
# sketch/LANG-REFINEMENT-PLAN.0.md), and each engine carries it out by
# that match. The match has no text of its own: canon, the hash form, a
# refusal and a loss report all write keyed under its own name.
# Each expectation is what both engines answer. Columns:
# name<TAB>mode<TAB>src<TAB>expect, with data before expect in the
# Canon writes the call the document wrote, its default left out where
# it is `any`, and never the match that carries it out.

column3: a: { &: keyed(re("^env_"), string, nil), env_name: prod }
a: { &: keyed(re("^env_"), string) } & { &: match(key(0), re("^env_"), string, any) }
a: { &: keyed(re("^env_"), string) } & { &: keyed(re("^env_"), string, any) }

column1: # The hash form writes keyed too, so a keyed call and the match that
# carries it out are two documents with two hashes.

column1: # A key the pattern admits is held to the schema; any other is held to

column3: a: { &: keyed(re("^env_"), string), env_name: prod, other: 1 }

env_a: keyed(re("^env_"), string, integer)\nb: keyed(re("^env_"), string, integer)

column1: # A seal is unchanged (ruling 19): a spread declares no key, so a closed
# map and a type's instance refuse a key that only the pattern admits,
# and a type that takes patterned keys is held open.
